title: Add geo-constraint enforcer, KMS claim proxy, and audit clarifier
author: Marisa Chen
release_notes: Add new GeoConstraintEnforcer middleware to validate per-request jurisdiction claims.
Introduce KMSClaimProxy to prefer region-anchored CMKs and record provenance in audit headers.
Add audit clarifier that normalizes and redacts region-sensitive fields for downstream log consumers.
description: Context: Several customers and internal audits called out ambiguous region headers and cases where KMS calls used global keys instead of region-bound CMKs, making it hard to prove data residency. This PR introduces three coordinated server-side components to tighten residency guarantees and improve audit signals: 1) GeoConstraintEnforcer - request middleware that validates a request's jurisdiction claim against route-level policy and RBAC v2 decisions; 2) KMSClaimProxy - a small routing shim that selects CMKs with region affinity and emits a signed KMS-origin header; 3) AuditClarifier - a post-ingest transformer that canonicalizes audit fields, strips PII from region assertions, and adds provenance tags. Motivation: Provide a pragmatic, opt-in guardrail that prevents accidental cross-region key usage and yields high-fidelity audit records for compliance reviews without changing customer-facing APIs. Design highlights: - GeoConstraintEnforcer integrates with the policy decision point (PDP) and the RBACv2 attribute-mapper. It runs early in the request path and can operate in shadow mode via feature flag (feature.geo_enforcer.shadow=true). It enforces: per-route allowed regions, operator-scoped overrides, and tenant-level residency preferences. - KMSClaimProxy wraps existing KMS client calls. It consults a small preference table (config/kms_region_prefs.json) keyed by tenant and service, attempts to use a region-anchored CMK, and falls back to a global CMK only when a safe-failover predicate is satisfied. When a region-anchored CMK is used, the proxy adds X-Redwood-KMS-Origin: region:<zone> and X-Redwood-KMS-Proof: <short-hmac> headers (HMAC using service key) to the request context so the audit pipeline can assert provenance. - AuditClarifier runs in the audit-ingest path and performs: canonicalization of region labels (us-west-2 -> US-WEST-2), redaction of tenant-ids from freeform claims, and insertion of kms_provenance tags when present. It also emits a small compatibility shim to keep older downstream consumers working. Rollout plan: - Step 0: feature flags default to off. - Step 1: Deploy KMSClaimProxy in shadow mode; collect metrics on fallback rate and latency. - Step 2: Enable GeoConstraintEnforcer in shadow (record violations but do not block). - Step 3: Toggle enforcement for a small subset of internal tenants; monitor alerts and runbook. - Step 4: Gradually widen enforcement, enable AuditClarifier, and promote KMSClaimProxy from shadow to active. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for policy matching and enforcement matrix added (pkg/enforcer/*). - Integration test suite simulating mixed-region tenants added to infra/ci/integration/kms_region_matrix_test.go. - Load test (bench/perf/kms-proxy-latency) to validate that proxy adds <= 2ms median latency at 95th percentile. - Backwards compatibility tests for audit downstream consumers. Migration & config: - Added config/kms_region_prefs.json (sample) and a new admin UI toggle (console feature flag) to manage shadow/active modes. - Database migration: none (proxy uses existing tenant metadata). Security review: Privilege separation retained; KMSClaimProxy runs with the same KMS principals as before and does not broaden permissions. The added provenance headers are HMAC-signed to prevent spoofing. Observability: - New metrics: kms_proxy.fallback_rate, geo_enforcer.violation_count, audit_clarifier.redaction_rate. - Tracing spans added for the proxy; token-level traces show region decision. CI: build and unit tests passed; integration flakiness resolved by increasing test timeouts in infra CI. Known limitations: - Edge-case: very old tenants without region metadata will default to global CMKs until admin opt-in. - Proof header is short HMAC for size reasons; full non-repudiation requires later ledgering work (follow-up ENG-6902).

review_comments: Jon Ortiz: Can the enforcer be bypassed by setting a custom X-Region header? Make sure we canonicalize and only accept PDP-validated claims. Suggested: drop raw header passthrough and rely on PDP attribute.
Author (Marisa Chen): Good point; updated geo_enforcer.go to canonicalize headers and only accept 'claimed_region' from PDP when present. Added unit test for header spoofing.
Priya Patel: Is there an RBAC matrix for operator overrides? We need explicit auditing when operator escalation occurs.
Author (Marisa Chen): Added operator override audit event and increment geo_enforcer.operator_override_count metric. See clarifier changes to include operator_override=true in the record.
Eve Nakamura: KMS HMAC key rotation — how do consumers validate proof after rotation? We should publish key id in header and rotate gracefully.
Author (Marisa Chen): Proxy now emits X-Redwood-KMS-Proof-Key: <kid> and rotation doc updated. Consumers validate using current and previous KIDs for a 24h window.
